### Model Architecture Analysis & Implementation Feasibility

| Model Architecture | Summary of Performance Across Papers | Implementation & Reproduction Feasibility |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Standalone Pre-Trained Transfer Learning CNNs**<br>*(Inception-v3, ResNet-50, Xception, DenseNet, EfficientNet)* | • Inception-v3 matched 21 board-certified dermatologists, attaining an AUC of 0.96 for keratinocyte carcinoma and 0.94 for melanoma.<br>• Fine-tuned ResNet-50 achieved 93.2% multiclass accuracy across seven HAM10000 categories.<br>• Fine-tuned Xception and Inception-ResNet-v2 achieved 94.3% accuracy and 95.1% AUC.<br>• ResNet-50 and EfficientNet achieved 94.1% accuracy with >90% clinical hallmark spatial alignment via Grad-CAM.<br>• Systematic reviews confirm transfer learning CNNs consistently outperform handcrafted methods and reliably achieve >90% mean accuracy and >95% ROC-AUC. | **Very Easy**<br>Standard architectures and pre-trained ImageNet weights are natively available in PyTorch, torchvision, and timm. Primary evaluation benchmarks (HAM10000, ISIC archive) are public. Only standard transfer learning classification heads and basic data augmentation pipelines are required. |
| **Deep & Heterogeneous CNN Ensembles**<br>*(VGG16 + Inception-V3 + ResNet-50; DenseNet-201 + ResNet-101 + EfficientNet-B4; Collective Voting)* | • Multi-backbone collective voting delivered a 3.8% accuracy gain over the single best standalone network.<br>• VGG16, Inception-V3, and ResNet-50 ensemble achieved 93.8% accuracy, 94.2% sensitivity, and 93.4% specificity on HAM10000 and ISIC sets.<br>• Weighted DenseNet-201, ResNet-101, and EfficientNet-B4 ensemble yielded multiclass AUC > 0.95 and reduced false negatives in early melanoma.<br>• Review syntheses show fine-tuned ensembles reliably maintain >95% ROC-AUC across benchmark repositories. | **Easy to Moderate**<br>The base CNN backbones are standard off-the-shelf models, and ensemble logic (soft voting, weighted averaging, or stacking) is simple to implement. However, reproducing the full pipeline requires 3× to 4× the compute, memory, and training time needed for standalone networks. |
| **Hybrid CNN Feature Extractors with Classical Classifiers**<br>*(ResNet-18 + MobileNet concatenated features + SVM)* | • Achieved 92.87% maximum overall accuracy on the ISIC 2019 dataset when combining deep features with an SVM classifier following active contours and CLAHE contrast enhancement. | **Easy to Moderate**<br>Extracting intermediate feature representations using PyTorch and passing them into an SVM (via scikit-learn) is straightforward. Active contour segmentation requires tuning energy and boundary parameters, though standard implementations exist in OpenCV and scikit-image. |
| **Vision Transformers & Cross-Attention Networks**<br>*(Dual-Scale Lightweight Cross-Attention ViT [DSCAT], Swin, ViT)* | • DSCAT reached 94.6% accuracy on ISIC benchmarks while reducing parameter count and FLOPs by ~60% compared to standard ViT baselines.<br>• Systematic meta-analysis confirmed hybrid CNN-transformers and self-attention models consistently exceeded 93% sensitivity across ISIC 2018–2020 benchmarks. | **Moderate to Hard**<br>While standard ViT and Swin backbones are accessible in Hugging Face and timm, custom dual-scale patch tokenizers and cross-attention fusion modules (DSCAT) require implementing specialized multi-scale attention heads if open-source model weights are unavailable. |
| **Soft-Attention Augmented Deep CNNs**<br>*(Attention gates integrated into ResNet and DenseNet)* | • Delivered an 89.2% balanced multiclass accuracy and a 0.96 mean AUC on minority diagnostic classes across severely skewed HAM10000 and ISIC 2017 datasets. | **Moderate**<br>Requires implementing additive or multiplicative attention gating blocks and hooking them into intermediate ResNet/DenseNet skip connections. The mathematical formulations are well-documented, but modifying standard backbone feedforward passes requires custom network subclassing. |
| **Custom Tailored CNN Backbones**<br>*(SkinLesNet, SCDNet)* | • SkinLesNet attained 98.3% training and 96.7% testing accuracy across seven lesion types on HAM10000.<br>• SCDNet attained 96.9% accuracy and 97.4% precision using modified residual bottleneck blocks. | **Moderate**<br>Network architectures (convolutional layers, batch normalization, residual bottleneck blocks) are simple to declare in Keras or PyTorch. However, training non-pretrained CNNs from scratch requires careful tuning of learning rate schedules, initialization, and regularization to match reported test scores. |
| **Lightweight & Dynamic Kernel CNNs**<br>*(Dynamic Kernel DK-CNN, Edge-Optimized MobileNet)* | • DK-CNN delivered 93.5% top-1 accuracy on HAM10000 while staying under 5 million parameters.<br>• Optimized MobileNet achieved 94.8% test accuracy while sustaining low-latency inference (<50 ms per image) on resource-constrained embedded edge devices. | **Moderate (Edge MobileNet: Easy; DK-CNN: Hard)**<br>MobileNet variants reproduce quickly via pre-built depthwise separable layers. In contrast, DK-CNN requires implementing dynamic kernel generation conditioned on input scales, which can necessitate specialized convolution wrappers or custom CUDA operations if not open-sourced. |
| **Multimodal Adaptive Fusion Architectures**<br>*(CosCatNet)* | • Achieved superior multi-label AUC and F1-scores compared to single-modal baselines and conventional late-fusion methods on the 7-Point Checklist and Dermofit datasets. | **Hard**<br>Requires access to paired clinical macroscopic and dermoscopic datasets (Dermofit requires an academic license agreement). Implementing multi-stage adaptive feature fusion, cosine-similarity loss, and uncertainty estimation mechanisms demands substantial custom loss and pipeline engineering. |
| **Spatiotemporal / Sequential Hybrid Networks**<br>*(Unified Attention Network: EfficientNet + LSTM + MRFs)* | • Achieved 93% multiclass accuracy in differentiating nodules, melanoma, and basal cell carcinoma, substantially improving temporal disease monitoring over static image baselines. | **Hard**<br>Demands sequential/longitudinal lesion data tracked over time, which is rarely included in standard public dermoscopy archives. Coupling spatial CNN feature extraction with recurrent LSTM layers and Markov Random Field (MRF) graphical models introduces complex multi-step objective optimization. |
| **Domain Knowledge & Decision-Tree Hybrid CNNs**<br>*(Inception-v3 + Clinical Decision Trees & Expert Rules)* | • Attained 92.4% diagnostic sensitivity on clinical datasets from PUMCH, matching or exceeding the performance of intermediate-level clinical dermatologists. | **Hard**<br>While Inception-v3 is standard, the structured dermatological expert rules and decision trees require formal clinical ontologies. Furthermore, the evaluation was conducted on non-public hospital clinical datasets (PUMCH), preventing direct public reproduction. |
| **Wavelet-Augmented Convolutional Networks**<br>*(Gabor Wavelet-augmented CNN [G-CNN])* | • Achieved 91.8% diagnostic accuracy on ISIC 2017, significantly reducing feature overlap between seborrheic keratosis and malignant melanoma. | **Moderate**<br>Gabor filter bank math is well-defined and can be generated with SciPy or OpenCV. Integrating fixed or learnable multi-frequency Gabor filters into the initial convolutional layers of a deep network requires writing custom initializers or forward-pass filtering hooks in PyTorch. |
| **Handcrafted Feature Classifiers**<br>*(SVM, Random Forest, k-NN with EMD, LBP, Fractal Dimensions, GLCM)* | • Hierarchical k-NN with color histograms and GLCM achieved 88.5% sensitivity and 90.1% specificity.<br>• Ensemble ML (RF, SVM, k-NN) using 2D Higuchi surface fractal dimensions and color clusters yielded 96.2% sensitivity and 95.8% specificity on PH2 and MED-NODE.<br>• Multi-resolution EMD + LBP with SVM reached 95.3% accuracy.<br>• Systematic survey across 120+ studies confirmed handcrafted ML models generalize less effectively than deep CNNs across large-scale benchmarks. | **Moderate to Hard**<br>Classifiers (SVM, k-NN, Random Forest) are readily available in scikit-learn. However, the handcrafted feature pipelines (2D Higuchi fractal dimensions, empirical mode decomposition, GLCM texture matrices) require intricate digital signal/image processing that is computationally intensive, unstandardized across libraries, and hypersensitive to segmentation preprocessing. |

### Paper-by-Paper FPGA Implementation Difficulty (FINN on PYNQ-Z1 vs. hls4ml — Sorted Easiest to Most Difficult)

| Paper Title | Model Performance | Difficulty to Implement Using FINN for PYNQ-Z1 *(Unofficially Re-Enabled in Settings)* | Difficulty to Implement Using hls4ml |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| SkinLesNet: Classification of Skin Lesions and Detection of Melanoma Cancer Using a Novel Multi-Layer Deep Convolutional Neural Network | 98.3% training accuracy and 96.7% testing accuracy across seven distinct skin lesion types (HAM10000). | **Moderate**<br>Well-suited to FINN on PYNQ-Z1: a sequential Conv/BatchNorm/ReLU/MaxPool/FC topology compiles cleanly once re-implemented and retrained in Brevitas (e.g., W2A2–W4A4), with PYNQ-Z1 re-enabled in settings and folding tuned to XC7Z020 resources. | **Moderate**<br>Standard Conv2D, BatchNorm, Pooling, and Dense layers are fully supported in Keras/QKeras/HGQ (`io_stream`, `Resource` strategy). Primary effort is quantizing and pruning feature maps/FC layers to fit within XC7Z020's ~630 KB BRAM and 220 DSPs. |
| Multiclass Skin Lesion Classification Using a Novel Lightweight Deep Learning Framework for Smart Healthcare | 94.8% multiclass test accuracy with low-latency inference (<50 ms/image) on resource-constrained embedded edge devices (HAM10000). | **Moderate**<br>Strongest architectural match for FINN: depthwise separable convolutions and global average pooling align with FINN's MobileNet-v1 support. Requires Brevitas QAT (≤4-bit), width/channel pruning to fit XC7Z020's 140 BRAMs (no URAM), and re-enabling PYNQ-Z1 in settings. | **Moderate to Hard**<br>Depthwise separable convolutions and GAP are supported via `io_stream` (Keras/QKeras/HGQ). Fitting an image-resolution MobileNet on XC7Z020 still requires width-multiplier reduction, pruning, and low-bit quantization to keep all weights on-chip. |
| SCDNet: A Deep Learning-Based Framework for the Multiclassification of Skin Cancer Using Dermoscopy Images | 96.9% classification accuracy and 97.4% precision across multiple dermoscopy image repositories (HAM10000). | **Moderate to Hard**<br>Standard convolutions and residual bottleneck additions are natively supported in FINN (via Brevitas QAT). Requires careful FIFO depth sizing across skip connections to prevent streaming deadlocks, low-bit quantization (2–4 bit) for XC7Z020 BRAM, and re-enabling PYNQ-Z1 in settings. | **Moderate to Hard**<br>Conv2D, BatchNorm, and residual `Add` layers are well-supported in `io_stream` mode. Key challenges are compressing channel widths/parameters via QKeras or HGQ and tuning `ReuseFactor` to fit XC7Z020 LUT/BRAM/DSP budgets. |
| Gabor wavelet-based deep learning for skin lesion classification | 91.8% diagnostic accuracy, significantly mitigating feature overlap between seborrheic keratosis and melanoma (ISIC 2017). | **Moderate to Hard**<br>Fixed multi-frequency Gabor filter banks can be precomputed on the ARM PS or folded into quantized fixed-weight first-layer Conv2D kernels in Brevitas. Downstream CNN layers compile cleanly in FINN if kept compact enough for XC7Z020 resources. | **Moderate to Hard**<br>Fixed Gabor filters can be implemented as a frozen initial `Conv2D` layer (fixed-point `ap_fixed` weights) or offloaded to the ARM PS, with downstream Conv/Dense layers synthesized via `io_stream` assuming compact QKeras/HGQ dimensions for XC7Z020. |
| A comprehensive analysis of deep learning and transfer learning techniques for skin cancer classification | 92.87% maximum overall accuracy concatenating ResNet-18 and MobileNet features with an SVM classifier post-contrast enhancement (ISIC 2019). | **Hard**<br>Active contours, CLAHE preprocessing, and the SVM classifier cannot be compiled by FINN and must run on the ARM PS. While ResNet-18 and MobileNet layers map to Brevitas/FINN, fitting both backbones on XC7Z020 requires heavy pruning, low-bit quantization, or sequential bitstream swapping. | **Hard**<br>CLAHE, active contours, and non-linear SVM lack native support (must run on PS or via custom HLS; linear SVM can map to a single Dense layer). ResNet-18 + MobileNet (~15M combined params) exceed hls4ml's on-chip XC7Z020 memory budget without drastic pruning/distillation. |
| Skin Lesion Classification Based on Surface Fractal Dimensions and Statistical Color Cluster Features Using an Ensemble of Machine Learning Techniques | 96.2% sensitivity and 95.8% specificity discriminating malignant melanoma from benign atypical nevi (PH2, MED-NODE). | **Not Suitable / Very Hard**<br>Purely classical ML (Random Forest, SVM, k-NN) and handcrafted features (2D Higuchi fractals, color clusters); FINN only compiles quantized neural networks and cannot accelerate this pipeline. | **Moderate to Hard (Partial via Conifer)**<br>2D Higuchi fractal and color cluster extraction must run on the ARM PS or custom HLS. Random Forest compiles cleanly via hls4ml's sister package **Conifer** (BDT/RF support moved from hls4ml to Conifer), whereas non-linear SVM and k-NN lack native support and require custom HLS or PS execution. |
